Pulls show docker-style progress and skip layers already stored; DNS works in containers on hosts whose `/etc/resolv.conf` is an absolute link; and the sandbox keeper no longer carries the caller's environment.

## Pull progress, and no re-download of stored layers

`xcrunner pull`, and a `run` or `create` that has to pull, report on stderr as docker does: `<tag>: Pulling from <repo>`, one line per layer (Pulling fs layer, Download complete, Already exists, Pull complete), a live bar on a terminal, then the Digest and Status lines. The result line on stdout is unchanged, `pull -q` turns progress off, and the API stays silent unless a caller sets `Runtime.progress`. A layer already extracted in the store is no longer downloaded again.

## DNS when /etc/resolv.conf is an absolute link

Some VPN clients make `/etc/resolv.conf` an absolute symlink. The keeper mounted it after `pivot_root`, where the link no longer resolved, so names did not resolve in ns containers. `/etc/resolv.conf` and `/etc/hosts` are now resolved on the host before the pivot.

## The keeper's environment

Pid 1 of the sandbox is the keeper, and any process inside can read `/proc/1/environ`. The keeper now starts with the loader and locale variables only, not the caller's whole environment.
